blocks.text: Welcome to Competen.

Competen is a digital healthcare education, professional development and organisational competency platform designed to support learning, professional growth, quality improvement and the development of healthcare services.
These Terms of Use govern access to and use of the shared Competen platform, including its account services, identity infrastructure, common technologies and platform-wide functionality.
Competen's principal product families include:

items: Competen Enterprise: Organisational workforce development, learning, competency management and related institutional services.
Competen Individual: Personal learning and professional development, including Scholar and Professional.
Competen Practice: Healthcare practice and related operational services.
Competen Recruitment: Professional career and recruitment services, as and when made available.

blocks.text: Individual products may have additional terms governing their specific activities.
By creating an account, accepting these Terms or using the relevant services, you agree to comply with the applicable provisions.
Where you access Competen through an employer, educational institution or other organisation, additional organisational agreements and policies may apply.

This foundation may include identity management, authentication, access control, user profiles, artificial intelligence services, learning infrastructure, competency records, digital evidence and the Competen Passport.

An organisation's authority over its own records does not automatically give it access to an individual's private learning materials, personal AI interactions or independently maintained professional records.
Similarly, a user's personal account does not automatically confer authority to modify organisational records.
Users must use Competen lawfully, responsibly and consistently with its intended purposes.
Users must not:

items: Access another person's account or records without authorisation.
Misrepresent qualifications, credentials, professional registration or competency.
Upload information they are not entitled to disclose.
Introduce malicious code or attempt to compromise platform security.
Circumvent access controls, usage limits or payment requirements.
Use the platform to harass, defraud, discriminate unlawfully or otherwise harm others.
Present AI-generated material as independently verified professional evidence.
Use educational content as a substitute for required clinical supervision or professional judgement.

blocks.text: Competen may investigate suspected misuse and take proportionate protective action.

blocks.text: Competen respects the privacy and data-protection rights of people who use its services.
This Privacy Notice explains how personal information is collected, used, stored, disclosed and protected when individuals interact with the shared Competen platform.
It applies principally to shared platform activities, including identity, authentication, personal accounts, access permissions, security, common technology services and related administration.
Specific products may provide additional Privacy Notices.
Competen Holdings is intended to operate the shared platform infrastructure.
Its legal role as a data controller, processor or joint controller for particular processing activities will depend on the purpose of processing and the relevant contractual arrangements.
For example, an organisation may determine the purposes of processing its workforce information, while Competen provides technology to process that information on its behalf.
The final allocation of responsibilities will be identified in the applicable legal and contractual documentation.
Depending on the services used, we may collect:
Identity and contact information: Name, email address, telephone number, country, account identifier and voluntarily supplied profile details.
Authentication and security information: Account status, authentication events, sign-in history, security logs and information necessary to protect accounts.
Access and organisational information: Product memberships, authorised roles, HQ appointments, institutional relationships and service entitlements.
Platform activity: Service interactions, technical diagnostics, access events, audit records and information needed to operate the platform.
AI service metadata: Where AI is used, operational information such as model, token usage, cost, status and applicable user or service attribution.
Communications: Requests for assistance, account-related correspondence and service notifications.

Billing information: Subscription and transaction records where paid services are introduced. Payment-card information, if applicable, will be handled according to the actual payment-provider arrangement.
Product-specific learning, professional and clinical information is addressed in additional notices.
We process personal information for purposes including:

items: Managing subscriptions and transactions where applicable.

blocks.text: We will not use personal information for unrelated purposes without an appropriate lawful basis and required notice or permission.
The lawful basis depends on the processing activity and applicable law.
Potential bases include performance of an agreement, compliance with legal obligations, consent where required, and other grounds permitted by law.
The final processing-purpose and lawful-basis mapping must be approved before publication.
Where consent is relied upon, it must be informed, specific and appropriately recorded.
Accepting contractual Terms does not automatically constitute consent to every optional processing activity.

items: Authorised Competen personnel who need it for their duties.
Competen operating entities under appropriate arrangements.
Organisations with which a user has an authorised relationship.
Technology providers acting under applicable contractual safeguards.
Payment or communication providers where necessary.
Regulators or public authorities where disclosure is legally required.

blocks.text: A user's personal learning information is not automatically available to their employer merely because the employer also uses Competen.
Disclosure must follow applicable product permissions, lawful purposes and contractual responsibilities.
We do not sell personal information to advertisers.

The final published notice must confirm which providers are active in production, the information each receives, relevant processing locations and applicable contractual safeguards.

Access to information is limited according to authorised responsibilities.
No digital system can guarantee absolute security. Suspected incidents will be assessed and managed according to applicable security and legal requirements.
Subject to applicable law, individuals may request:

items: Withdrawal of consent where consent is the lawful basis.
Restriction or objection where legally available.
Copies or export of relevant personal information where applicable.

blocks.text: Welcome to Competen Individual.
Competen Individual is a lifelong healthcare education, learning, competency development and professional growth platform.
It comprises two interconnected experiences:
Competen Scholar supports students and other learners through academic study, revision, knowledge assessment, clinical reasoning exercises and preparation for professional practice.

Competen Professional supports healthcare professionals through continuing professional development (CPD), personal development planning, competency evidence, professional credentials, reflective practice and career progression.

Both experiences operate through a shared Competen identity and may use common services, including personal profiles, learning history, artificial intelligence infrastructure and the Competen Passport.
These Terms govern your use of Competen Individual and supplement the applicable Competen Holdings Platform Terms of Use.

Where the two sets of Terms address different matters, the Holdings Terms govern shared platform services and these Terms govern Individual-specific services. Any material inconsistency will be resolved according to applicable law and the final legally approved contractual arrangements.
Competen Individual uses a shared platform operated by Competen Holdings.
Competen Professional is intended to be operated by Competen Holdings.
Competen Scholar is intended to be operated by a separately incorporated subsidiary of Competen Holdings.
The legal responsibilities of the respective operating entities will be identified in the published legal documents.
A person using Professional must accept the applicable Holdings documentation.
A person using Scholar must accept the applicable Holdings documentation and any additional Terms issued by the Scholar operating entity.
Where both experiences are active, all applicable Terms must be accepted.
Competen Individual is intended for healthcare students, healthcare professionals and other eligible individuals engaged in relevant education or professional development.
During the initial pilot, access is by invitation only.
Users must have an authorised Competen account and an active entitlement to the relevant experience.
The initial Scholar pilot is restricted to individuals aged 18 or older.

Users must provide accurate eligibility information. Where an authorised administrator confirms eligibility, that confirmation does not relieve the user of responsibility for providing truthful information.
Competen may request additional verification where reasonably necessary.
Professional access does not require previous participation in Scholar.
Competen Individual uses the shared Competen authentication system.
Each person should ordinarily maintain one identity across Competen products.
During the invitation-only pilot, authorised Competen administrators may invite new users or grant access to existing Competen accounts.

An invitation does not guarantee continuing access. Access depends on successful authentication, invitation acceptance, applicable legal acceptance, entitlement validity and other relevant security controls.
Users must not transfer invitations, share accounts or use another person's identity.
Competen may refuse, suspend or terminate access where necessary to protect security, enforce eligibility requirements or comply with applicable law.
Competen Individual is designed to support continuity from education into professional practice and throughout a person's career.
A Scholar user may subsequently activate Professional without creating a separate Competen identity.
A Professional user may also activate Scholar for further education.
Where both experiences are active, the user may switch between them through the Individual application.
Graduation or activation of Professional does not automatically terminate an existing Scholar entitlement.
Personal learning history and other retained records are governed independently of whether a particular experience remains active.
Continuity does not mean that all information is automatically shared between experiences, organisations or third parties.
Competen Scholar provides tools for personal education, revision, knowledge development and preparation for healthcare practice.
Available capabilities may include:
Availability may vary according to the user's entitlement and the current product release.
Users may upload lecture notes, study materials and other content they are lawfully entitled to use.

Users must not upload identifiable patient information or confidential clinical records into Scholar's personal learning service.

Users must not upload content that violates copyright, confidentiality, privacy or other legal obligations.
Competen may refuse material that appears to breach applicable upload rules.
Automated screening is a safeguard but cannot guarantee detection of every prohibited identifier or disclosure.
Scholar may use AI to generate explanations, revision questions, feedback and educational clinical scenarios.
Such content is intended to assist learning and may contain errors, omissions, outdated guidance or misleading interpretations.
Users should compare important information against authoritative educational references, current clinical guidance and instructions from qualified educators.
AI-generated content must not be treated as independently verified clinical guidance unless it has completed an applicable review and approval process.
Clinical cases in Scholar are educational exercises.
A scenario generated from personal notes is not necessarily clinically reviewed.
Where reviewed content is available, its review or verification status will be identified.
Completing a scenario does not establish that the learner is competent to perform a clinical procedure or make an independent clinical decision.
Scholar may record answers, practice activity, revision history and learning progress.
Practice accuracy reflects performance on particular educational activities. It does not automatically demonstrate mastery, professional competence or readiness for unsupervised clinical practice.
Competen does not guarantee examination success, academic progression, admission, graduation or professional registration.
Competen Professional supports the organisation and development of an individual's professional learning and career information.
It may provide:

items: Professional portfolios and the Competen Passport.

blocks.text: Users are responsible for ensuring that their professional declarations are accurate and current.

Competen Professional may assist users in recording CPD activities and planning their professional development.

Where available, users may configure in-app and email reminders for dates they have recorded.

title: Competen Individual — Privacy Notice (Scholar and Professional)
preamble: Holdings operator: [Registered legal name to confirm]
Scholar operator: [Registered legal name or approved interim arrangement]

This working draft consolidates the prior sections. Legal counsel must confirm the bracketed facts, lawful bases, provider terms, data roles, retention periods and regulatory obligations before publication.

blocks.text: Competen Individual supports lifelong healthcare education and professional development. Scholar offers AI-assisted explanations, revision, practice questions and educational clinical reasoning. Professional supports CPD, development plans, reflections, credentials and competency evidence. Both share one identity and selected infrastructure, but personal information is not automatically shared between products or with employers. This Notice explains collection, use, disclosure, retention, security and rights. Read it alongside the Holdings Platform Privacy Notice and applicable Terms of Use.

Competen Holdings is intended to operate shared identity, authentication, profiles, entitlements, AI infrastructure, Passport and Professional. Scholar is intended to operate through a separately incorporated, majority-owned subsidiary. Controller and processor roles depend on actual processing decisions, not ownership alone. [CONFIRM registered names, numbers, addresses, controller allocation and intra-group agreement before publication.]

This Notice covers invited users of Scholar and Professional, shared Individual services and relevant Passport sharing. The initial pilot is invitation-only. Scholar pilot users must be at least 18. Professional does not require prior Scholar participation. Each experience requires its own entitlement and applicable legal acceptance. Younger-user services and public registration require separate review.

Account information includes name, optional given and family names, email, phone, country, identity identifiers, authentication status, invitations, entitlements and acceptance versions. Scholar may process uploaded notes, source passages, questions, responses, feedback, scenarios, revision schedules, recall ratings, progress and selected achievements. Professional may process profession, speciality, registration details, credentials, CPD hours, development needs, plans, reflections, evidence, renewal dates and reminder preferences. Passport data includes selected records, provenance, verification status and link-sharing controls. Operational data includes audit, security, diagnostic and AI usage metadata. Some information may be sensitive and require additional safeguards.

Information is obtained from users and their uploads, activity in the application, authorised administrators managing invitations, organisations issuing or verifying evidence, and technical service providers. Shared identity does not make records from one Competen product universally accessible to others.

We use information to provide secure access; deliver learning, AI explanations and revision; maintain CPD and professional records; enable selected Passport sharing; send essential notices and optional reminders; prevent misuse; preserve audit evidence; operate and support the platform; and comply with law. Private study material is not automatically contributed to shared libraries or distributed commercially.

Processing must have a lawful basis under applicable law, potentially including performance of a service agreement, legal obligation, consent where required or another lawful ground. Sensitive information may require additional conditions. Terms acceptance is not blanket consent to optional AI or other activities. [LEGAL ACTION: approve purpose-by-purpose lawful bases and sensitive-data conditions.]

Scholar may send a user question and the passages selected as most relevant from their notes to an AI provider to generate explanations, questions or feedback. Professional may process information relevant to a user-requested plan, learning suggestion or reflection draft. The current architecture uses Anthropic's API; confirm provider entity, contractual terms, retention and transfers. Competen does not use private uploads to train its own AI models, and the current Scholar service does not authorise third-party model training of private uploads. Explanations are not saved as permanent learning records by the current explain step; generated questions and source passages may be saved. Shared AI usage logs retain model, tokens, cost, operation and status rather than question/answer text. Transient processing and provider retention may still occur. Persistent Personal AI conversational memory is currently off. AI output is not clinical advice, professional verification or a substitute for supervision.

Upload only material you have permission to use. Do not upload identifiable patient information or confidential clinical records to Scholar. Users may attest that files contain no patient identifiers and that they have upload rights. Automated screening cannot identify every prohibited disclosure. Users remain responsible for confidentiality, copyright and professional obligations.

Private Scholar notes, question answers, practice accuracy, schedules and personal AI interactions are not automatically accessible to employers or institutions. Individual study records are not automatically placed in Enterprise learning analytics. Disclosure requires user authorisation, another lawful basis or legal obligation.

Professional records may be self-declared, self-directed, document-attached, organisation-issued or independently verified. The status and source must remain clear. Institutions may retain authority over records they issue; an individual's personal copy does not authorise altering institutional history, and an institution does not automatically gain access to unrelated private Individual records.

Eligible Scholar achievements are excluded by default and can be selected individually. Removing a Passport selection does not delete the underlying study history. Time-limited, revocable sharing links may disclose selected records to anyone holding a valid link. Revocation blocks later access through the link, not copies already obtained. Private notes, answers, accuracy, AI conversations and confidential reflections are excluded by default. An active link does not establish credential verification.

Enterprise, Practice, Recruitment and Individual share identity infrastructure but have separate permissions. Institution-issued evidence may appear in a person's Passport, and users may choose to disclose eligible records. Future integrations require lawful grounds and governed technical controls; no unrestricted sharing is implied.

Information may be shared with authorised personnel, applicable Competen operating entities, relevant issuing or verifying organisations, contracted hosting, storage, authentication, AI, email and payment providers, and authorities where required by law. Current architecture includes Supabase, Vercel and Anthropic API services; the actual production entities and subprocessor terms must be confirmed. We do not sell personal information to advertisers.

Providers may process information outside Uganda. Competen must assess destinations, legal transfer conditions, contracts and safeguards before publication. [LEGAL ACTION: complete international transfer mapping and provider assessment.]

Retention depends on purpose and legal requirements. Accounts, invitations, uploads, revision history, CPD, credentials, Passport shares, AI metadata, consent records, audit logs and backups may have different periods. Entitlement expiry does not automatically erase historical records. [REQUIRED: insert approved retention schedule or meaningful category-specific criteria, including backups.]

Users may request deletion of eligible information, subject to lawful restrictions. Turning off AI help does not automatically delete saved materials, questions or learning history. Removing a Passport achievement does not erase study activity. Revoking a link cannot retract information recipients already copied. Closing an account or ending access does not automatically erase legally retained evidence. Where information cannot be deleted, Competen will assess the request and explain the applicable reason where lawful.

Users may edit permitted personal details. Email changes use verified authentication procedures. Institution-issued credentials and competency decisions may require issuer correction. Original records and authorised corrections may be retained for audit integrity rather than silently overwritten.

Scholar practice indicators and Professional AI suggestions do not independently determine professional registration, employment, academic qualifications, competence or fitness to practise. Any future consequential automated decisions require assessment of applicable safeguards, human review and challenge rights.

Appropriately authorised operational data may be analysed to improve reliability. Private uploads are not automatically shared with other learners, used for model training or added to a verified knowledge library. Any future optional contribution requires a distinct lawful basis and applicable permission. Anonymisation must be meaningful; pseudonymised information remains personal data where re-identification is possible. Identifiable research may require ethical approval.

Safeguards may include secure authentication, product entitlements, server-side checks, Individual row-level security, restricted administration, audit trails, private storage, controlled Passport links and backup/recovery.
